title: The seawall, alone
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Tuesday, after the shop. The seawall. Ten feet of wall where she sat. Wood sits in his spot, not hers. The dog goes to hers and lies down on it. The strip draws the ten feet exactly.

panels.composition: The seawall at evening, rain hatched, WOOD sitting in his spot. Ten feet of empty wall. BARNABY walking the ten feet.

image.prompt: a young man in a chore coat sitting on a seawall in vertical rain with ten feet of empty wall beside him and a small dog walking along it, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The dog lying down on the far spot. Hers.

image.prompt: a small dog lying down on a section of seawall ten feet from a seated young man, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The ten feet. Exactly. The strip drew it with a ruler.

image.prompt: close on ten feet of wet concrete seawall between a seated figure and a lying dog, drawn precisely, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The wall. The two spots. The bay. The strip draws the distance exactly because it's the only thing about the evening it can be exact about.

image.prompt: a young man and a small dog at opposite ends of a measured stretch of seawall above a gray bay in rain, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen over rough blue pencil; xerox grain; stark spotting; rain in frantic vertical hatching (Arc 1's aesthetic)

notes: Ten feet, drawn with a ruler. The dog takes her spot.
